items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1976-02-13
items.q: Johnny Wiggs once said that Bix had to have a beautiful soul

ctx.x: You see, you never find it in a piece like this, for instance.

No, and something I might point, I might bring out here, John, is you asked me in which way did he influence music a lot. I think, as I would think right now, his use of his intonation, like his blues, his flats, flattening a note, and using it to a blues note. You see, for instance, like a... He got the most out of a blue note like that, taking and flatting it, and really, really making it something that he gave it so much feeling. You know, I mean, it's hard to explain it, but the pleasure to just hear it.…

items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I knew of Johnny and had met him and certainly talked with him many times. I can't recall playing any early jobs with Johnny until our association in 1946 at WSMB radio station.

ctx.x: Did you work with Johnny Harmon in those days?

I can't remember too well if I worked any jobs with Johnny in those days. I knew of Johnny and had met him and certainly talked with him many times. I can't recall playing any early jobs with Johnny until our association in 1946 at WSMB radio station.
The Lesley Hems records, they sound like nickels, you know. He made two tunes, I forget the date, but the late 20s, Johnny Harmon's Bayou's
